record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: For n ≥ 2, does there exist a smooth compact connected hypersurface M^{2n−1} in R^{2n} whose characteristic flow is minimal, meaning that every orbit is dense in M^{2n−1}?

evidence.quote: When n ≥ 2 can one find M2n−1 ⊂ R2n, a C∞-compact connected hypersurface, such that on M2n−1 the characteristic flow is minimal (every orbit is dense) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 2. The characteristic line field on a smooth orientable hypersurface M^{2n−1} ⊂ R^{2n} is defined as follows: identify R^{2n} with its standard symplectic structure ω = Σ_{i=1}^{n} dx_i ∧ dy_i, and at each point p ∈ M let L_p ⊂ T_p M be the one-dimensional kernel of the restriction ω|_{T_p M} (which is well-defined because T_p M has codimension 1 in a symplectic vector space). The characteristic flow of M is the (unparametrized) flow generated by any nowhere-vanishing smooth vector field that spans this line field. The flow is called minimal if every one of its orbits is dense in M.

Question: For every integer n ≥ 2, does there exist a C^∞-smooth, compact, connected hypersurface M^{2n−1} ⊂ R^{2n} whose characteristic flow is minimal?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of whether a smooth compact connected hypersurface in R^{2n} (n ≥ 2) can carry a minimal characteristic (i.e., Reeb-type) flow appears in standard lists of open problems in Hamiltonian/contact dynamics and is widely cited as still open. Recent work on Reeb dynamics, the Weinstein conjecture, and entropy bounds for Reeb flows does not resolve the existence of a minimal example in this setting.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
status_evidence.snippet: List includes the question of existence of a smooth compact connected hypersurface in R^{2n} with minimal characteristic flow for n ≥ 2.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Spectral characterizations of Besse and Zoll Reeb flows
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on Reeb flows on restricted contact type hypersurfaces of symplectic vector spaces concerns spectral and periodic-orbit characterizations, not minimality.
status_evidence.claim: Recent Reeb-flow literature does not exhibit a minimal characteristic flow on a closed hypersurface in R^{2n}.
